answer: Each identity posts a 120-credit bond on a nebula registry and faces a prism check that splits its credential into three strands: funding source, work record, and key control, each verified by a panel before the epoch horizon. Panels publish strand results, and a mismatch burns the bond. The k-th fake from one operator costs 120+30(k-1) credits in correlation fees, so 1,000 fakes lock 15,105,000 credits. A rented-strand ring fails: a borrowed work record carries another key and trips the mismatch. One honest identity posts 120 once and reclaims it after the horizon.
